title: Googlebook "Better Together" phone features don't work with Samsung at launch
gist: Google's new Googlebook laptops require Android 17 for their 'Better Together' phone integrations, which currently work only with Pixel phones; even Samsung's Android 17 flagships are unsupported at launch, undercutting Google's premium-laptop push.

insights.claim: At launch, Googlebook phone-integration features (app streaming, file access, notification mirroring, cross-device continuity) only work with Pixel phones, despite Google marketing the laptops as working with 'your Android phone right out of the box.'
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Google's laptop push is effectively a Pixel-ecosystem play at launch, narrowing its addressable market.
insights.quote: For now, Googlebooks will only play nicely with your phone if you have a Pixel.

insights.claim: Google confirmed its 'Better Together' features are unsupported even on Samsung's latest Android 17 phones such as the Z Fold 8, with support promised in 'the coming weeks.'
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Excluding the largest Android OEM at launch is an execution misstep that could slow Googlebook adoption.
insights.quote: Google representatives have since confirmed that these “Better Together” features are not currently supported on even the latest Samsung phones.

insights.claim: The author judges that launching Googlebooks without Samsung support, and without disclosing it publicly, is a poor start for Google's refreshed laptop effort since Samsung is by far the largest Android OEM.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Ecosystem-lock features can backfire when the dominant OEM partner is left out.
insights.quote: Launching Googlebooks without Samsung support, and not being clear about that in any public statements, is not a great start for Google’s refreshed laptop effort.

insights.claim: Other OEMs lag on Android 17: Motorola's 2026 phones shipped on Android 16 and still await 17, OnePlus (which scaled back in several markets) is still testing it, and Xiaomi has it on some high-end devices but Googlebooks are absent from most of its core markets.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: OS-version fragmentation directly caps the Googlebook-compatible phone base for months.
insights.quote: Motorola released its 2026 phones with Android 16, and they’re still waiting on a final update to version 17.

insights.claim: Google had largely neutralized Android version fragmentation by moving features into Google Play Services and a modular system layer, making OS-exclusive features rare; Googlebook support is a notable reversal of that pattern.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Tying a hardware product to a new OS version reintroduces the fragmentation cost Google spent years engineering away.
insights.quote: there are very few features exclusive to new versions today, but Googlebook support is apparently one of them.

insights.claim: The Googlebook platform likely appeals most to existing Pixel owners, implying the laptop effort reinforces Google's first-party hardware ecosystem rather than the broad Android base.
insights.speaker: Ryan Whitwam
insights.so_what: Googlebook success may track Pixel market share more than Android share.
